# D14 — Split protocol: one headline axis, two declared stress axes

**Status:** Accepted (2026-10-19)
**Supersedes:** the implicit assumption that "Bemis-Murcko scaffold split" is a
single well-defined protocol.
**Evidence:** `docs/DATA_LEAKAGE_AUDIT.md` (generated by
`molmetal/scripts/wf_a51_leakage_audit.py`); `docs/ALIGNED_COMPARISON.md` §1-§2.

## Context

The 2026-10-19 audit measured molecule-level leakage at **0.00 %** in every
active split, and then found that three splits claim more chemical separation
than they deliver:

| Split | Claimed | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| CFM v3/v4 | strict Bemis-Murcko, 0 scaffold leak | 0 at the shipped key, but **73.7 % of test rows and 79.6 % of val rows** share a desalted stereo-blind ligand scaffold with train |
| MoleculeNet | Bemis-Murcko scaffold split | key kept chirality until 2026-10-19; now stereo-blind and bit-exact with `astartes` (`include_chirality=False`). The shipped AUCs predate the fix |
| Pt 4-cell | `scaffold_70_10_10` | `scaffold_id = _stable_hash_int(smiles, 10**8)` — a molecule-level hash; **41.9 % of test rows** share a desalted scaffold with train. A real split is now opt-in (`bemis_murcko_70_10_10`, 0.0 % overlap) |

The literature does not support "always scaffold split" as the remedy:

- **Krasnov 2026** (the source paper for MetalCytoToxDB, J. Med. Chem.
  `10.1021/acs.jmedchem.5c02755`) uses **DOI-grouped 10-fold CV**, not a
  scaffold split. Comparability with the published 0.810 ± 0.024 depends on
  reproducing that grouping.
- **Guo, Hernandez-Hernandez & Ballester 2024**, *Scaffold Splits Overestimate
  Virtual Screening Performance*: for VS-like ranking, scaffold splits remove
  the actives' own chemotypes from training and are **pessimistically biased**;
  random/grouped splits better match deployment.
- **Coverage bias in small molecule ML**, Nat Commun 2025
  (`10.1038/s41467-024-55462-w`): the question is whether test is covered by
  train, not whether a scaffold is shared.
- **Cyclic-peptide benchmark**, J Cheminform 2025
  (`10.1186/s13321-025-01083-4`): scaffold splits cut training diversity and
  make models generalise *worse* — a different question, not a stricter one.
- **BOOM** (arXiv 2505.01912) defines OOD in property space via KDE and
  deliberately avoids scaffold splits.

The two positions reconcile once the question is named. A scaffold split is
the right protocol for "can this model generate a **new ligand chemotype**",
and the wrong protocol for "can this model rank **new complexes from new
papers**".

## Decision

1. **Predictive headline stays DOI-grouped 10-fold.** This is the
   Krasnov-comparable axis and the deployment-matched one for VS-like ranking.
   The random-CV scaffold overlap (74.8-85.7 % of test rows) is reported as a
   property of random CV, never as a scaffold-generalisation estimate.
2. **The generative line declares a ligand-scaffold axis.** CFM novelty claims
   are only meaningful under a **desalted, stereo-blind** Bemis-Murcko key.
   Until the split is rebuilt, the measured 73.7 %/79.6 % overlap must be
   stated next to any generative quality number.
3. **MoleculeNet comparability uses the reference key.** The key must match
   `astartes`' default (`include_chirality=False`, no desalting) before the
   chemprop column is treated as like-for-like. The desalted number is a
   supplementary stress test, not the headline.
4. **Split changes are model-session work.** Re-splitting CFM, changing the
   MoleculeNet key and renaming the Pt strategy all invalidate trained
   artefacts. The audit wave changes **no** model, trainer, config or
   checkpoint. `TODO/risks.md` R9 tracks the handoff.
5. **Every scaffold claim names its key.** "0 scaffold leak" is meaningless
   without the key. `p0_scaffold_zero_leak` now prints the chemical-axis
   overlap alongside PASS for exactly this reason.

## Consequences

- No reported number changes as a result of this ADR. What changes is the
  label attached to three splits, plus one new measured number at launch time.
- The CFM generative metrics remain measured on a split whose val set shares
  79.6 % of its rows' ligand scaffolds with train. That is now stated wherever
  the audit is cited; it is not fixed.
- Aligning the MoleculeNet key is expected to **lower** the bbbp/bace/clintox
  AUCs (PROJECTED: separating a stereo-pair is an information leak, and the
  aligned split closes it; the size of the drop is not measured until the
  re-run). hiv is unaffected — its scaffolds carry no stereocentres. This is
  the cost of removing an unfair advantage over the chemprop baseline, and it
  must be reported as a protocol correction, not a regression.

## Update 2026-10-19 (Wf-A53) — what moved after this ADR

The ADR above records the audit state. Since then, four of the handoff items
are closed without changing any reported number:

- **CFM v5 is launchable.** `configs/cfm_5metal_v5_full.yaml` pins v5 and sets
  `n_train: 0` / `n_val: 0` (<= 0 means "every embeddable row"). The default
  config is unchanged, so the 2026-10-17 checkpoint remains reproducible.
- **The test split has a reader.** `wf_a53_eval_cfm_test_split.py` is
  read-only and reports `HELD_OUT` / `NOT_HELD_OUT` by comparing the evaluated
  split against the checkpoint's own training file. For the v3-trained
  checkpoint on v5-test the verdict is `NOT_HELD_OUT` (609/848, 71.8%).
- **Decode connectivity is measured.** `evaluate_decode_ratio` now returns
  fragment statistics via `stats_out`, and the trainer writes
  `decode_single_fragment_ratio` / `decode_fragments_mean` to the CSV and
  event stream. MEASURED: 256/256 decodes, 0/256 single-fragment, mean 16.7
  fragments — the ratio alone was uninformative.
- **The two mislabels are loud at runtime**, not only in this document.
- **The MoleculeNet key is aligned** to `includeChirality=False`
  (bit-exact with `MurckoScaffoldSmiles(includeChirality=False)` on all
  85,174 rows across the four tasks). This is a code change, so it belongs
  here rather than in the "still open" list: the *key* is fixed, the
  *numbers* are not. MEASURED test-set turnover across the five seeds is
  63.6-76.5 % (bbbp), 59.3-83.5 % (bace) and 39.3-87.0 % (clintox); hiv is
  0 % because none of its scaffolds carry stereocentres. Consequently hiv's
  shipped 0.7900 remains valid, while bbbp/bace/clintox are on a different
  test set and their shipped AUCs must be re-run before citation
  (`metrics/by_metric/moleculenet_scaffold_key_alignment.json`).
- **BindingDB loads again.** The symlink target had been truncated to zero
  bytes on 2026-09-30; it now points at the 990,630-row TDC export and the
  loader accepts both header spellings.
- **Pt 4-cell has an honest split available.** `--platinai-split-strategy
  bemis_murcko_70_10_10` is a real Bemis-Murcko scaffold split (desalted,
  stereo-blind, `largest_first`, seed 0) with MEASURED **0.0 %** test-row
  scaffold overlap at 13,148 / 1,056 / 2,108 rows. The legacy
  `scaffold_70_10_10` remains the default — it is a SMILES hash and still
  reproduces the audited 41.9 % — so no shipped checkpoint is invalidated
  by this change. `metrics/by_metric/platinai_4cell_scaffold_split_alignment.json`.

- **The aligned key was re-run end-to-end (2026-10-19, 40 min).** The full
  four-task × five-seed PA14 512/4 protocol completed with pre-flight PASS and
  20/20 fresh per-seed outputs. MEASURED
  (`metrics/by_metric/moleculenet_auc.json`, `split_key:
  bemis_murcko_stereo_blind`): bbbp 0.9025 ± 0.0350, bace 0.7422 ± 0.0828,
  hiv 0.7976 ± 0.0170, clintox 0.7957 ± 0.1075, mean 0.8095. The
  pre-alignment 512/4 artifact is annotated `superseded`; the columns are not
  paired (59-87 % of test molecules differ) and must not be differenced
  row-by-row. hiv moved +0.0087 on an identical split, which bounds the
  training-nondeterminism floor.

Still open, because each requires a re-run rather than a code edit:
a Pt 4-cell model trained on the scaffold split, and a CFM checkpoint trained
on v5.
